newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metalworkers reach pay deal in south region.
newsitem.headline: German metalworkers reach pay deal in south region.

text.p: Metal and engineering employers in the southern German region of Nordwuerttemberg said on Wednesday they had agreed a 1997 wage deal for the some 600,000 workers in the industry there.

Under the accord, which mirrors others signed in the sector in all major respects, employees will continue to receive sick pay at full salary, an entitlement that was under threat from a law passed in October allowing employers to cut sick pay.

Nordwuerttemberg is among the last major metal and engineering regions to reach a 1997 wage agreement. Accords have now been signed for some three-quarters of the 3.2 million workers in the west German industry.
Under the agreement, workers will receive a 1.5 percent pay rise in 1997 and a further 2.5 percent increase the year after.
In return for allowing sick pay to be retained at 100 percent of salary, companies will be allowed to make small cuts in other areas, such as existing holiday or Christmas bonuses.
Metal and engineering workers across the country had threatened all-out strikes next year if employers did not back down on plans to cut sick pay.
